records.title: MRT Putrajaya Line: staged opening and a connected journey
records.answer: The Putrajaya Line is an operating regional railway whose usefulness depends on transfers, station access and dependable service. Its opening dates establish delivery, while its equipment descriptions explain what must keep working.
records.scope: One 57.7-kilometre MRT line from Kwasa Damansara to Putrajaya Sentral, including its staged opening. It crosses a regional corridor; it is not confined to either Kuala Lumpur or Putrajaya. Future stations and other MRT lines are not additional delivered components or counted identities here.
records.stage: Passenger opening documented in 2022 and 2023; technical capabilities described. No comparable recurring-performance series admitted.

identity_decision.rationale: The owner names a continuous line and supplies distinct opening accounts for its first section and complete service. The earlier SSP designation, migrated stations and two opening stages belong to the same project. It is counted once, separately from the two municipal places, without reusing a country acquisition docket.

timeline.event: Implementation approval reported by the project overview.
Final railway-scheme approval reported; month precision is retained.
Groundbreaking at the Putrajaya Sentral site reported.
First section opened to the public.
Full line launched, infrastructure handed to Rapid Rail and public entry recorded.

sections.heading: One line across a regional corridor
sections.text: MRT Corp describes a 57.7-kilometre route linking Kwasa Damansara and Putrajaya, with elevated and underground sections. Its overview distinguishes 36 operating stations from five stations planned for future use. These are different categories: a future station shown along an alignment does not add another functioning stop. The corridor crosses the boundaries used for the two city accounts below. That matters when assessing coverage, because neither city alone represents the railway’s service area. The overview’s roughly two-million corridor population is a catchment description, not a count of passengers carried.

sections.heading: A first section with existing connections
sections.text: The first section opened on June 16, 2022 between Kwasa Damansara and Kampung Batu. MRT Corp describes three stations migrating from the Kajang Line and a cross-platform transfer at Kwasa Damansara. It also records thirteen new feeder routes and KTM connections at Sungai Buloh, Sri Damansara Timur and Kampung Batu. This opening therefore changed a network, rather than merely adding isolated track. For a passenger, the practical value of those connections depends on the walk, the wait and the onward service. The opening configuration is historical, not a guarantee of today’s timetable.

sections.heading: The full opening and the operating handover
sections.text: The March 16, 2023 launch account explicitly records completion of the project and infrastructure handover to Rapid Rail. It also describes public entry that afternoon, making this a post-event opening account rather than a forecast. The handover identifies a useful institutional boundary between infrastructure delivery and passenger operation. The launch’s free-ride promotion belonged to March 2023 and is not a continuing fare offer. Subsequent service quality belongs to the operating record, not to the ceremonial date.

sections.heading: Accessible equipment and usable journeys
sections.text: The technical description lists tactile paving, ramps, accessible toilets, low counters and lift controls designed for wheelchair users. Those features describe provision, not continuous availability. In practical terms, a step-free trip requires the relevant equipment and the connection beyond the station to work together. A lift outage can matter even when trains remain frequent. The next useful comparison is therefore station-specific access over time, including recovery from faults, rather than a single inventory of installed features or an undifferentiated claim that the whole network is accessible.

sections.heading: Power and control remain service dependencies
sections.text: MRT Corp describes driverless trains managed from an operations control centre and electricity supplied through bulk and traction substations. These are linked parts of the service, not independent substitutes for one another. The technical page also describes backup power, but that design description does not establish uninterrupted passenger operation during a real outage. Editorially, the important distinction is between possessing protective equipment and demonstrating recovery under operating conditions. Comparable incident records would need to identify the affected part of the system, the duration and the consequence for journeys.

sections.heading: Editorial test for the next operating account
sections.text: A useful follow-up would join train reliability, station accessibility and transfer performance without collapsing their denominators. Count a cancelled train separately from a passenger’s failed connection, and retain the station and time window for an unavailable lift. Compare like periods, explaining changes in service frequency or network coverage before attributing a difference to the project. Passenger totals can show use, but they do not alone establish time savings, affordability or reduced traffic. Those outcomes require their own definitions and comparison designs. This approach would turn an opening chronology into a defensible account of the railway people actually experience.

next_artifacts: A dated operator service and station inventory separating active stations from future provision.
Comparable train, lift and transfer performance with stable periods and passenger exposure.
A current feeder and fare account, separately dated from the historical opening promotions.

records.title: Kuala Lumpur: city planning and everyday mobility
records.answer: Kuala Lumpur’s transport outcomes depend on municipal planning and street management as well as regional rail. Its city plan, bus responsibilities and traffic-control remit provide distinct ways to understand those dependencies.
records.scope: The Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur administered by DBKL, counted as one municipal place. Excludes Greater Kuala Lumpur, the whole Klang Valley and Putrajaya; regional railway and highway service areas do not redefine this boundary.
records.stage: Municipal functions and adopted strategic-plan status described; future targets and operating responsibilities remain separate from verified outcomes.

identity_decision.rationale: DBKL identifies the Federal Territory as its municipal jurisdiction, and its planning department uses that same geographical scope. The place is not the wider metropolitan labour market, a railway corridor or every road monitored by a control centre. It is counted once and separately from Putrajaya, with no historical country docket reused.

timeline.event: City status recorded in DBKL’s municipal history.
KLCCC’s official indexed FAQ dates the transport-management hub to this year.
Structure-plan gazette date reported in the library synopsis; underlying instrument not inspected.
Separate structure-plan effective date reported in the same synopsis.

sections.heading: A municipal boundary within a larger urban region
sections.text: DBKL’s background account identifies it as the local authority for the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur. It assigns functions spanning public sanitation, waste, planning, environmental control and urban infrastructure, and records city status on February 1, 1972. This is the place boundary used here. Regional commuting and rail services extend beyond it, so a metropolitan result should not automatically become a municipal result. The distinction helps readers ask who can act on a problem: a street-maintenance issue, a railway operating issue and a regional land-use question may require different responsible institutions.

sections.heading: Strategic policy and detailed development control
sections.text: The planning department distinguishes a structure plan’s strategic direction from the local plan’s detailed land-use and intensity controls. DBKL’s library synopsis reports that the 2040 structure plan was gazetted on October 19, 2023 and became effective on November 23. Those are separate dates, reported by a synopsis rather than independently read from the gazette instrument. The hierarchy matters for interpreting a development claim: a citywide mobility objective is not permission for a particular parcel. A named project still needs the applicable local controls and its own approvals before a policy ambition can become an implementation account.

sections.heading: Green and mobility goals need different measures
sections.text: The 2040 framework connects mobility with inclusion, green space, climate resilience and spatial development. Its green targets include 200 kilometres of park connectors and 50 percent canopy coverage. These remain targets for 2040, not present achievements. They also describe different things: route length, shade, and access to useful destinations cannot be substituted for one another. An editorial comparison should ask whether a connection reaches homes and public transport, whether it remains usable in heat or rain, and how its maintenance is funded. A total length alone cannot answer those neighbourhood questions.

sections.heading: The street network around the railway
sections.text: The transport department’s official indexed responsibilities include GoKL bus management, traffic-flow proposals and maintenance of pedestrian, cycling and micromobility facilities. Direct retrieval of that page failed, so this is a bounded account of published responsibilities rather than a live inspection. These roles show why a regional railway is only one part of a city journey. A station can be open while the approach requires a difficult crossing or an inconvenient connection. Responsibility statements identify where to seek an implementation record; they do not establish that every facility is complete or every advertised service has run.

sections.heading: Traffic control has a defined institutional reach
sections.text: KLCCC describes traffic monitoring and signal control, but its official indexed FAQ distinguishes that remit from toll-road concessionaires’ own systems. That boundary is more useful than treating one control centre as the operator of every road in the metropolitan region. It also matters when matching an incident to a responsible agency. A published camera or control-system description is not an observed reduction in congestion. The source’s differing road-length figures are not used as a single coverage total here. Current journey conditions would require time-specific information, not a general description of the centre.

sections.heading: Editorial test for a joined-up city account
sections.text: The next account should connect a named neighbourhood, a real destination and the agencies responsible along the journey. Record walking conditions and transfers alongside scheduled and actual public transport, with dates that let readers distinguish a temporary disruption from a structural access problem. Keep strategic targets in view, but measure delivery through completed facilities and services rather than the number of plans published. For green space, pair physical extent with usable access and maintenance. Such a bounded comparison would explain where a transport investment changes daily life without attributing all metropolitan growth or every local improvement to that investment.

next_artifacts: The exact applicable local-plan and parcel records for any named development claim.
Dated GoKL and walking/cycling implementation records, with route and neighbourhood scope.
Comparable canopy, park-access and journey measures with explicit baselines and city boundaries.

records.title: Putrajaya: rail access, managed water and municipal services
records.answer: Putrajaya combines an administrative-city plan with regional rail access, local buses and a constructed wetland system. Those systems have different operating responsibilities and should be assessed through the services they provide.
records.scope: The Federal Territory of Putrajaya, counted as one place, not twenty separate precincts or the whole Kuala Lumpur urban region. The regional MRT line and the lake catchment are connected systems rather than alternative municipal boundaries.
records.stage: Historical territorial development and rail opening documented; water-system functions and municipal responsibilities described. Archived bus plans are not current service verification.

identity_decision.rationale: Putrajaya Corporation’s official historical account identifies the planned administrative city and its declaration as a Federal Territory. Its precincts, wetland cells and transport interfaces are parts of one place account, not separately counted cities. The identity is distinct from Kuala Lumpur and from the regional MRT project, without reuse of a historical country docket.

timeline.event: Perang Besar site selection recorded in the Corporation’s later historical account.
Revised master-plan approval reported with month precision.
Federal-territory declaration described in the 2014 retrospective.
Scheduled Rapid Bus start in the archived Nadiputra announcement, not a post-event completion receipt.
Full MRT opening account includes a journey to Putrajaya Sentral.

sections.heading: An administrative city with a distinct identity
sections.text: The Corporation’s 2014 history traces site selection at Perang Besar to June 1993, followed by a revised master plan in February 1995. It describes detailed planning for twenty precincts and the federal-territory declaration on February 1, 2001. This chronology separates the making of the city from later additions to its services. The precincts are internal parts of one place, not twenty new place identities. Equally, the administrative role should not be confused with the whole metropolitan economy around Kuala Lumpur. A municipal assessment needs its own population, service boundaries and reporting periods.

sections.heading: Water infrastructure within the urban landscape
sections.text: The Corporation describes a constructed system of 24 wetland cells, including the central wetland, upstream of Putrajaya Lake. Vegetation, sedimentation and controlled water movement contribute different treatment functions; habitat, flood detention and recreation are also part of the design. This makes the water landscape infrastructure as well as public space. Its performance depends on maintenance and incoming pollutant loads, not simply on the presence of planted water. The system description is not a dated water-quality result. An operating account would need sampling locations and comparable periods to show what enters the system and what reaches the receiving lake.

sections.heading: A regional railway meets a local destination
sections.text: MRT Corp’s full-opening account ends with the launch journey arriving at Putrajaya Sentral. That establishes a named interface between the regional railway and this place, not complete access to every precinct. A passenger still needs an onward connection to the actual destination. Editorially, the useful unit is therefore the whole journey rather than arrival at the terminus. Walking routes, bus waits and opening hours can change the usefulness of a railway connection even when the train itself operates as planned.

sections.heading: Nadiputra has a separate service history
sections.text: The archived municipal notice announced Rapid Bus operation under the Nadiputra name from January 1, 2023, with seven routes and cashless payment arrangements. Its displayed notice window runs from December 29, 2022 to March 31, 2023. Those dates do not turn the announcement into a current timetable or a post-event operating receipt. The notice identifies the service transition and the operator to consult for updated information. For evaluating rail access, the relevant next evidence is an actual dated connection to a precinct destination, including the waiting time and the service available outside peak commuting hours.

sections.heading: Digital functions require accountable operations
sections.text: The Corporation assigns ICT infrastructure, application maintenance and management of the Putrajaya Command Centre to its corporate-services organisation. Its substantive departmental text is in Malay even on the English-navigation page. The roles connect digital systems with ordinary municipal duties, including customer service and performance management. They are responsibilities, not evidence of application uptime or successful incident handling. A useful operational account would trace a reported problem through acknowledgement, agency assignment and resolution, while preserving privacy. That would show whether a digital interface helps residents obtain a service rather than merely recording another deployed technology.

sections.heading: Editorial test for an integrated place profile
sections.text: Follow a small set of real service questions across their institutional boundaries. Can a resident complete an evening return journey? Does a water-quality change appear upstream as well as downstream, and over what period? Does a municipal report reach the team able to fix the problem? Each question needs its own observation and denominator. Avoid combining them into a synthetic smart-city score that conceals the distinction between equipment, plans and outcomes. A stronger profile would retain the urban design history while adding repeated, dated records of the services residents and visitors can actually use.

next_artifacts: A current Nadiputra service and transfer account tied to named precinct destinations.
Dated wetland and lake monitoring with sampling locations, methods and maintenance context.
Municipal service-resolution and application-availability records, with personal data excluded.
